newsitem.title: USA: Texaco creates $200 million pipeline system.
newsitem.headline: Texaco creates $200 million pipeline system.

text.p: Texaco Inc. said Friday a subsidiary is creating a 1,300-mile pipeline system worth more than $200 million to transport gasoline, diesel and jet fuels from Texas' Gulf Coast to terminals in northern and western Texas, Oklahoma and Kansas.

When complete, the system will have a combined capacity of more than 200,000 barrels per day, providing economical transportation from the Gulf Coast's refining and import centres to various inland markets, the company said.
The 1,300-mile common carrier pipeline that is the backbone of the new system is scheduled to begin operations in January.

The subsidiary, Texaco Trading & Transportation Inc., declined to discuss terms of the various deals planned to create the new system. But it would have a total value of "over $200 million," said Dan Nerbonne, vice president for business development.
Texaco said it has begun exclusive negotiations with Koch Pipeline Co. LP and Koch Refining Co. LP to form a joint venture that will own the new refined products system.
This is expected to involve a combination of assets and cash, Nerbonne said, declining to discuss specifics.
Texaco Trading spokeswoman Linda Padon said the two companies already own the Chase Pipeline, which will link the new system to Denver, which it links with El Dorado, Kansas.
Texaco said it has purchased an existing 16-inch pipeline from Corsicana, to Midland, Texas, which the planed joint venture with Koch expects to extend 275 miles to El Paso.
It said 360 miles of crude oil pipelines linking Houston to Wichita Falls, Texas, via Corsicanna will be converted to product pipelines.
The company said it expects to link these lines to Duncan, Okla., with a new pipeline which connects to existing piplines to Oklahoma City; Cushing, Okla.; Tulsa and El Dorado.
Connections to other pipelines on both the northern and western legs are anticipated, Texaco's statement said.
Texaco said a long-term product supply agreement with Pride Cos. LP calls for products to be delivered to Pride at its existing terminals at Albilene and Aledo, Texas.
Texaco Refining & Marketing Inc., another Texaco Inc. subsidiary, has committed to take 25,000 to 30,000 barrels per day of product requirements from the system.

Texaco Trading's existing East Houston Station will be the origin point for products from Houston-area refineries and bulk terminals and, through pipeline connections, from the Port Arthur-Beaumont and Corpus Christi, Texas refining centres.
Texaco's stock edged up $1.375 to $112.25 on the New York Stock Exchange.
